title: Wasteland
build: Electronic Arts disk release, two double-sided disks as four G64 side images; play copies made with the game's own Copy utility

records.c: Operand of the CMP #imm at $9007, written at $8FEF (agent 7's attribute scan of a check square's pairs): the record offset of the attribute the player chose, compared with the second byte of each kind-2 pair.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $900B, written at $8FF4: the offset of the check pair the attribute scan is looking at ($0A, $0C, ...); $9020 reloads it so the scan returns Y on the matching pair.

Shows map message number record byte +2 of the square at ($5F) in the message area, if that byte is non-zero ($BE1E: show_map_message). Second entry $9029, inside the BIT at $9028, does the same with byte +3. Callers of $9026: the check-square handlers $8C7D, $8F50, $8F63.
Entry hidden in the BIT $03A0 at $9028 (LDY #$03): shows map message number record byte +3 of the square at ($5F) when it is non-zero ($BE1E). Reached from $8DD3 (JMP), $8EE4 and $8F2D.

A = the record byte at ($5F)+Y shifted right five times (the LSR here, four more at $A5FC): the kind of a check pair. The check-square code dispatches on it ($8E52): 0 skill, 2 attribute, 3 party size, 4 cash, any other value an item that must be carried and loses a charge. Y kept.
A = the record byte at ($5F)+Y AND $1F: the low five bits of a check pair's first byte, the difficulty of a skill or attribute check (for a skill, 0 means owning it is enough, $8EAE). Y kept.

Applies the check square's effect, record bytes +8 and +9 at ($5F), to party member A: nothing when +8 AND $7F is 0. The field is +8 AND $7F, a character-record offset. The amount is +9 AND $7F as it stands when +8 has bit 7 set, otherwise that many d6 ($BDC4); it goes to $6F/$70 ($0401). Bit 7 of +9 means subtract. Runs in slow scroll at the speed in $906A (2 at first; $907A keeps whatever speed the player set with the cursor keys for the next effect), applies it through change_member_field, then restores the scroll mode and speed (slow_scroll_restore).

Operand of the LDX #imm at $9069: the scroll speed apply_square_effect uses for its text, 2 as loaded; $907C stores the speed $0F there after each effect, so a speed the player changes with the cursor keys sticks for the next effect.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9073: the party member apply_square_effect works on, stored at $9039.
Operand of the LDX #imm at $9075: the character-record offset of the field the effect changes (record byte +8 AND $7F), stored at $904B.

Changes field X (a character-record offset) of party member A by the amount in $6F/$70; Y bit 7 set subtracts, clear adds. Subtracting: CON (+$1D) is damage, printed and applied by $A85B (amount in A/X, member in Y) with $C8 = 1 and $A0 = bit 0 of the square record's byte 0 during the call; cash (+$15) goes through spend_cash ($03CE: nothing taken when the member is short); any other field loses the low byte of the amount and stops at 0. Adding: experience (+$21) gains it through $03DD ($0825, saturating); any other field gains the low byte unless the sum passes 255, in which case it is left unchanged.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $908E: the direction byte (record byte +9; bit 7 set subtracts), stored at $9088 and tested by the BPL after the load.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $9092: the character-record offset of the field being changed, stored at $9082 and reloaded at $90D5.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $90BA: the party member, stored at $9085, handed to the damage routine $A85B in Y.
Applies the check square's effect (apply_square_effect) to every member of the current party in turn, 1 to $07. Used when the square record's flag byte has bit 4 set ($8CE6, $8F1A).
Operand of the LDY #imm at $90FE: the member apply_effect_to_all has just done, stored at $90F7; the loop goes on while it is below or equal to $07.

Y = the offset of the check pair that passed (+$0A, +$0C, ...): skips the pairs to their $FF terminator and returns Y = terminator + 1 + (pair - $0A), the offset of that pair's two-byte square change in the list that follows the terminator (same order, two bytes each). $0A00 then applies it. Callers: $8C89, $8F56.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9115 and check_change_offset's scratch byte: the pair offset it was given (stored at $9108), then the terminator offset + 1 (stored at $911B) added to it at $911F.
A = record byte +8 of the square at ($5F) AND $7F, the field offset of the check square's effect (0 when it has none, Z set); Y = 8.

A = record byte +0 of the square at ($5F) with Y = 0: the check square's flag byte, tested bit by bit by its handlers (bit 1 at $8DCB, bit 3 at $8C83 and $8F4C, bit 4 at $8CE2 and $8EC6, bit 5 at $8EF2 and $8F0B, bit 2 at $8F20, bit 6 at $8E33, bit 7 at $8F75).

Shows map message number record byte +3 of the square at ($5F) in the text window (text_window_select, print_map_message) in slow scroll at speed 2, waits four delay rounds (delay_x_times), then falls into slow_scroll_restore. Callers: $8CDC, $8EDA, $8F17.

Puts back the scroll speed $0F and the slow-scroll flag $A8 that slow_scroll_on saved into the operands of these two LDA #imm ($9145, $9149). Reached at the end of square_message_slow and by JMP from apply_square_effect ($907F).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9144: the scroll speed $0F as it was before slow_scroll_on, stored at $9154.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9148: the slow-scroll flag $A8 as it was before slow_scroll_on, stored at $914F.

Saves the slow-scroll flag $A8 and the scroll speed $0F into slow_scroll_restore's operands, then sets $A8 = 1 (text pauses line by line and the cursor keys change the speed, engine $253A) and the speed $0F = X.

The last test of a move into the square at column X, row Y ($AD8B, after the type 2 and type 10 handlers): $B12D gives its type and points ($5F) at its record. Type 11: map message +0 is shown when non-zero, and unless record byte +1 is negative the square change at +1/+2 is applied to that square ($0A00); carry set, the party stays. Type 4 (an object square, whose tile is record byte +1 AND $7F, engine $0B8E): passable, carry clear, unless +1 has bit 7 set; then the same with the change at +2/+3, carry set. Any other type: carry clear.
Entry for type 11, hidden in the BIT $01A2 at $9179 (LDX #$01): the square change is read from record offset 1. Type 4 arrives at $9177 with offset 2.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $9184: the record offset of the square change bump_blocking_square applies (1 for type 11, 2 for type 4), stored at $917C.
Operand of the LDX #imm at $918B: the column of the square being moved into, stored at $915E.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $918D: the row of the square being moved into, stored at $9161.

Square type 5, a loot bag (entry 5 of the square-type table at $ACF3, run through $ACDB). ($5F) is the bag's record: +0/+1 the square change made once it is empty, then entries of an item byte and a count byte from +2 to a $FF. Each entry is fixed in the record the first time a bag is opened, and the map is written back with it: an item byte 1-$5D with bit 7 clear names a class and becomes a random item of that class (count_items_of_class, then the n-th match) with bit 7 set; $5E (Cash) becomes $DE and the two bytes after it are each rolled from 1 to themselves (a 16-bit amount, so a cash entry takes three bytes); a count with bit 7 set becomes 1 to (count AND $7F). Counts entries in $4D and non-empty ones in $4E (both from 1, for the list), $D1 past the last, then goes on at loot_pick_member.

Operand of the LDY #imm at $91CD, loot_square's offset of the entry being fixed (from +2 in steps of two, one more for a cash entry), stored at $919E and $9258, read back at $91F2, $91FC, $920B, $92A0, $92C7.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $91E1: the item number loot_square's random pick is counting through (from 1 up), stored at $91DB and stepped at $91DE.
Operand of the CMP #imm at $91E9: the entry's item byte AND $7F, the class searched for while fixing a bag ($91B1), then the item chosen from the list ($9260).

Second half of loot_square: shows the roster, asks 'Who wants loot?' (game message 16) and takes a member (pick_member); left-arrow clears the message area ($AC8C) and returns carry clear. A member who is not conscious gets message 17 ('can't get any') and the question again. Then the bag is listed (loot_list_setup, list_show_page) and list_choose takes an entry: left-arrow asks for a member again. Cash is added to the member (cash_add) and the entry emptied, with the byte after it set to $FF so it ends the list once the entry is two bytes again; an item goes to the first free slot with its record's byte 4 as the count byte (find_free_slot; 'You can't carry any more.', message 18, with a sound when full) and the entry's count drops by one. When an entry empties, $4E drops; at 1 (nothing left) the square change at record +0 is made (A = 0, $B105) and its carry returned.
Y + 1, then the record byte at ($5F)+Y becomes a random number from 1 to itself (random_1_to_a; 0 stays 0). loot_square calls it twice to roll a cash amount, low byte then high byte ($91BC).

A = an item class: returns A = the number of items from $5E (Cash) down to 1 whose class is A (record from $0BCD, then item_class), Z set when none. A = 0 returns $5E at once, a value loot_square never asks for (it skips entries whose byte is 0).
Operand of the LDA #imm at $92FB: count_items_of_class's item counter, $5E stored at $92F8, stepped down to 1 at $930A.
Operand of the CMP #imm at $9303: the class count_items_of_class is looking for, stored at $92EE.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $930F: count_items_of_class's tally of matching items, cleared at $92F3, stepped at $9307, returned in A.

Starts the loot list: direct output, game message 19 ('<name>, take an item' and the '#  ITEM' heading) through $7F44, the first entry on the page $4A = 1, and the list's per-line routine $47/$48 = loot_list_line.

Per-line routine of the loot list (vector $47/$48, called by list_show_page with A = entry k): reads entry k at record offset 2k. An empty entry (item 0) returns carry set and is not shown. Otherwise prints the line's label (list_line_label), the count right-aligned in four columns (for Cash, item $5E, the 16-bit amount, print_word_padded; also kept in $38 for the plural), a space and the item's name ($0BDC: engine message item + $24); carry clear.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $9345: the record offset of the entry loot_list_line is printing (2k), stored at $932F.
Operand of the LDX #imm at $934C: the item number loot_list_line is printing, stored at $9338, compared with $5E (Cash) and passed to $0BDC.

Turns the position records ($5B4F: 16 records of x, y, map, distance, four per party) into battle groups ($EE00 + $178*party + $5E*group, $BBC7). First pass: a group whose x/y/map matches a record ($9877) is swapped ($98CF) into the record's own slot (record n is party n/4, group n AND 3, $98C5). Second pass, for each record with no group yet: the group gets x, y, map and the distance in feet ($08F5); ($77) is pointed at the record of the square ($BB75); the monster numbers and counts of its three slots (record bytes 3/4, 5/6, 7/8) that still have bit 7 set are rolled once, 1 to n, and written back into the map; the encounter's message (record byte 2) and 'n <monsters> ... appear at d feet.' are printed ($BA8F); and every monster of each slot gets hit points: a quarter of the monster's 16-bit seed (monster record bytes 0/1) + 1-to-low-byte + 256 x 1-to-high-byte (random_1_to_a), one word each. Called by the Enc command ($B23D) after scan_for_encounters. Reselects the party it started with.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $9376: the offset (0-$3C, steps of 4) of the position record place_encounter_groups is working on; stored at $9373, $9383, $93BD, $93CE.
Operand of the CMP #imm at $93A4: the party of the battle group matched to the position record ($9877, stored at $939B); in the second pass the party of the record's own slot ($93EA).
Operand of the CPX #imm at $93A8: the group number to go with $93A5 (stored at $939E and $93ED).
Operand of the LDX #imm at $940F: the column of the position record's square (from $5B4F), stored at $938D and $93D9, for the distance $08F5.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $9411: the row of the position record's square (from $5B50), stored at $9393 and $93DF.
Operand of the LDX #imm at $9430: the monster slot (0-2) place_encounter_groups is rolling or filling with hit points; stored at $941F and $9459.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9488: the high byte of the monster's hit-point seed (monster record byte 1, $9EE6), stored at $9477.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $948C: the low byte of the monster's hit-point seed (monster record byte 0), stored at $9474.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $94AB: the offset of the hit-point word being written in the slot's sub-record (0, 2, 4, ...), stored at $9485.
A = party, X = group of the position record place_encounter_groups is on (offset $9377, through position_to_slot).

Looks for encounters around every party on the battle map $8D. A = 0 here; second entry $94CF (inside the BIT at $94CE) sets A = 1, which also draws each monster's tile on the calling party's view and redraws squares (the main loop's $ACA5, $B19B). Clears the 16 position records at $5B4F; $F4E1+party = the longest reach of the party's conscious members ($BC39: 15 melee, $FE a gun with rounds). Then for each party on that map it scans its 19 x 9 view ($02/$03, $54) for squares of class 3 or 15; an encounter there counts when the party can see it ($8347: no class 11 square on the line) and when the distance in feet ($08F5) is within its record byte 1, or within both the party's reach and record byte 0. Such a square is recorded for the nearest party that can engage it ($977E, $97D8), up to four per party, a nearer one replacing the farthest; moving a record restarts the scan. Ends at $9707.

Entry hidden in the BIT $01A9 at $94CE (LDA #$01): scan_for_encounters with drawing on: monster tiles ($5BF5 + monster kind) are drawn on the calling party's view and out-of-range squares redrawn ($9828).

Operand of the LDA #imm at $9501, a counter used three ways: the member (1-$07) whose reach is being tested ($94F1-$950A), the party (3 down to 0) in encounter_party_distances ($9783-$97CF), and a position-record offset ($9691, $96A8, $971F).

Operand of the CMP #imm at $9510: the longest reach found so far among the party's members ($9514); then reused for the distance in feet from the scanning party to the square ($95C4), read at $9613 and $9627.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9525: the party that called scan_for_encounters ($94E0); compared at $95D9 and $982F, reselected at $959D.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9536: the party being scanned, 0 to $0B; stored at $9533, stepped at $958D.
Operand of the CMP #imm at $953D: the battle map $8D the scan is for ($94E5); also compared at $974D and $9799, passed at $975B.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9599: set to 1 when a position record was moved ($9824) or a farther one replaced ($96FE); the scan then starts over.
Operand of the LDX #imm at $95FD: 1 when scan_for_encounters was entered at $94CF (draw monster tiles, redraw squares), 0 at $94CC; stored at $94D1, tested at $9828.

Operand of the LDA #imm at $9649: the party $97D8 chose last (nearest that can engage), stored at $9652 and $96C4. At $9649 it is loaded before this pass has stored it, so the compare with $964C and the distance kept in $9672 use the party chosen on the pass before (see the report).
Operand of the CMP #imm at $964B: the party whose four position records already hold this square (find_position_record, stored at $963C); compared again at $968C and $96A3.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9671: the distance kept with a new position record ($97F2 stores it at +3) and compared with the records already held ($9673, $96E6); stored at $964F and $96C1.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $9774: 1 once scan_for_encounters has stored a position record ($980B); cleared at $952B.
Operand of the AND #imm at $9776: 1 when a recorded encounter is hostile (record byte 9 bit 1 clear, $973E); cleared at $9709. With $9775 it makes the carry: clear when both are set.

For the square at $983F/$9841 and its record ($77): $F3E0+party = the distance in feet from each party 0-3 ($08F5), or $FF when the party does not exist, has nobody conscious, is on another map than $953E, has the square outside its view ($B119), cannot see it ($8347), or is farther than the record's byte 1 and its own reach ($F4E1+party). Reselects the party it started with.
Picks the smallest of $F3E0+party for parties 0 to $0B: A = that distance and X = the party; A = $FF (and X = 0) when every entry is $FF.
Fills position record Y ($5B4F+Y): column $983F, row $9841, map $09 and the distance $9672; sets the found flag $9775.
Clears the position record of the square at $983F/$9841 on map $09 (find_position_record) and asks for the scan to start over ($959A = 1).

Called for an encounter square that is out of range: with drawing on ($95FE) and the calling party scanning, redraws the square ($0B53) and returns carry clear; carry set for another party (go to the next square); with drawing off, carry clear.
X = the column, Y = the row of the square the encounter scan is on (the operands at $983F and $9841, stored at $955D and $9548).
Operand of the LDX #imm at $983E: the column of the square being scanned.
Operand of the LDY #imm at $9840: the row of the square being scanned.

A = map, X = column, Y = row: looks through the 16 position records at $5B4F for one with that square (an x of 0 marks a free record and never matches): carry set, A = its party (record number / 4) and Y = its offset when found; carry clear when not.
Operand of the CMP #imm at $9855: the column find_position_record looks for.
Operand of the CMP #imm at $985C: the row find_position_record looks for.
Operand of the CMP #imm at $9863: the map find_position_record looks for.

Y = a position record's offset: searches the battle groups of every party 0-3, groups 0-3 ($BBC7), for one whose x, y and map (+0, +1, +2) match the record: carry set with A = party and X = group when found, carry clear when not.
Operand of the LDX #imm at $9887: the position-record offset find_group_at_record compares with, stored at $9877.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $98A2: the party find_group_at_record is on (0-3), returned in A.
Operand of the LDX #imm at $98A4: the group find_group_at_record is on (0-3), returned in X.
A = party: Y = the offset of its four position records, from party_record_offsets (0, $10, $20, $30).
Four bytes 0, $10, $20, $30: the offset of each party's block of four position records at $5B4F, read by party_record_block.
A = a position-record offset (0-$3C): returns A = the party (offset / 16) and X = the group (offset / 4 AND 3) whose battle group the record belongs to.
Swaps the $5E-byte battle group of party A, group X ($BBC7, kept in $12/$13) with the group belonging to position record Y ($98C5), byte by byte.
Operand of the LDA #imm at $98DD: the position-record offset given to swap_group_records in Y, stored at $98CF.

Operand of LDA #imm at $A220, the end of member_attack's result loop (agent 8's routine from $9FA9), written at $A13D: the rounds the attack used, 1 for a single shot ($A0EB), 3 for a burst ($A0CE) or every round left for automatic fire ($A130, $BC73); $A220 hands it to $BC75, which takes it from the weapon's count.

Sets $E8 (a result of this attack has been printed, so the next starts with '...', $A230) and prints the name of band $A23F of the group at ($77): $9E5D with X = the band, the class word or the map's own name for it.
Prints game message 62, '...', when $E8 is set: the second and later results of one attack follow the first on the same line.

Carry clear when band $A23F of the attacker's target $A23A (a target code, 12*party + 3*slot + band) still has a living monster: splits the code (target_split $BDAF) and counts the band (band_alive $A83C), leaving $79/$7A on the band's 30-byte record.
Operand of LDA #imm at $A239: the attacking member's target code, written by member_attack at $9FEC (the order parameter AND $3F) and read back by it at $A00A, $A06C, $A0FC, $A11C and $A20C.

Operand of LDY #imm at $A23E: the band (0-2) member_attack is working on, written at $A05F and $A119 as it loops over the bands of the target's slot, read at $A072, $A096, $A122, $A12A and by print_band_name_marked ($A22A).

Counts the monsters of hit-list entry $A15B (the target at $7E06+entry) that took a hit this attack: the non-zero bytes among the ten counters at $7E12 + 10*entry. The count goes to $38 (singular or plural of the message) and to the operand at $A1E2 in member_attack.

Order 3, W)eapon, for member A (already the current character; the order table at $9F2E calls it): prints message 102 ('<name> swaps equipment.'), equips the slot in the member's order parameter ($8B),A through equip_toggle ($0389) and redraws the member's roster line.

After a battle round ($B8A9): for each party 0-$0B, notes in run_direction_by_record the direction of every conscious member with the Run order (4) and clears all orders; a party-move order (8) moves the whole party instead ($A323). Then each runner, in record order, is split off ($98F5) unless there are four parties already (message 88, 'couldn't run'; a party of one runs anyway), prints message 43 ('<name> runs.'), steps in its direction if the square allows (square_blocked $AD5B), and its square's action runs ($ACC1).

Eight bytes, one per character record 0-7 (0 unused): the direction (0-8, as the moves) in which that member runs at the end of this round, $FF for none. resolve_runs_and_moves fills it with $FF ($A27A), stores each runner's order parameter ($A2B0) and reads it back ($A2D2, $A2FB).
Order 5, E)vade, for member A: prints message 82 ('<name> evades.') and returns. The order code stays in the order table ($89) until resolve_runs_and_moves clears it after the round.

Order 6, L)oad/Unjam, for member A: a jammed weapon (bit 7 of its count byte, weapon_count $AC32) gets one unjam_weapon try, and stays as it is if that fails; a working one is reloaded with a clip of the item its record byte 7 names (find_item, reload_weapon), message 104 ('reloads'); otherwise message 65 ('has no more clips') or, with no clip item, 66 ('weapon can't be reloaded'). Redraws the roster line.
Operand of LDA #imm at $A38C: the member order_load_unjam is serving, written at its entry ($A383) and read back at $A396 and $A3B6.

Order 7, U)se, for member A: prints message 105 ('<name> uses...'), stops the picture's animation, calls the Use routine $8BEF with A = the high nibble of the member's order parameter, X = its low nibble, Y = the byte use_choice_by_record ($5BDB) holds for the member's record and $12 = the member (all chosen when the order was given), then runs the action of the party's square ($ACC1) and restarts the animation. Carry clear.
Operand of LDY #imm at $A3C7: the member order_use is serving, written at $A3BC and read back at $A3D4.
Operand of LDY #imm at $A3E1: the byte at $5BDB + the member's record number, written at $A3D1, passed to the Use routine $8BEF in Y (agent 10's $B787 stores it when the U)se order is given).

Order 1, H)ire, for member A, the hirer. Nothing when its target band is dead. Needs a free record (fewer than 7 in use, else message 95 'No room in roster.') and a group record ($77, byte +9) with bit 1 set and an NPC number in its high nibble. Copies that NPC's 256-byte record (word n of the map's list 17) to record $0A+1; unless its byte +$31 is 0 the hirer must then reach the NPC's (CHR+IQ)/2 + byte +$31 + rank with (CHR+IQ)/2 + CHR + rank + 2d6 (a roll under 5 fails and raises the NPC's bytes +$2B-+$2D). On success the NPC joins (records $0A and the party table), its message (+$30, map text) is shown, +$31 = the hirer's CHR, +$2B-+$2D drop once per 4 points of margin, its band leaves the fight and its items get full charges; on failure message 44 + 'the <band>' + 81 ('tries to hire ... but fails').
Operand of LDA #imm at $A44F: the hirer (a party position), written at order_hire's entry ($A3F1) and read at $A4B4, $A4ED and by hire_target_split ($A505).
Operand of LDA #imm at $A490: the hirer's CHR (+$14), taken at $A406 while the hirer is still the current character; stored in the new member's byte +$31 when the hire succeeds ($A494).
Operand of LDY #imm at $A4D3: the record offset of the item slot (+$BD to +$F7, step 2) whose count byte order_hire is filling with the item's full load (item record byte 4), written at $A4C8.
Splits the hirer's target code: Y = the hirer (hire_member_op), A = its order parameter AND $3F (member_target_code), then target_split ($BDAF) gives A = party, X = slot, Y = band.
Adds the current character's byte at record offset Y to the engine's second 16-bit accumulator $71/$72 (char_byte_y, then $07C6, which saturates). Used by order_hire for the NPC's byte +$31 and rank.
A = the current character's CHR (record byte +$14), X = 0: an operand for the engine's accumulator adds ($079D, $07C6).
A = the current character's record byte at offset Y, X = 0 (the high byte for the engine's 16-bit accumulator adds).
A = (CHR + IQ) / 2 of the current character (+$14 plus +$0F, the carry of the sum shifted back in by ROR), X = 0. Both sides of order_hire's test start from it.
Makes record $0A+1, the first character record not in use, the current character (select_character $0338). order_hire copies the NPC there before it knows whether it will join.

For member Y: its target code (member_target_code), split (target_split $BDAF), counted (band_alive $A83C). Carry clear when the target band still has a living monster, A = how many; $79/$7A is left on the band's 30-byte record.
A = member Y's target code: its order parameter at ($8B),Y AND $3F, 12*party + 3*slot + band (bits 6-7 hold the fire mode, member_fire_mode).

Ends member A's attack (member_attack jumps here, $9FE3): clears its order and order parameter. A weapon loaded with one shot (item record byte 4 = 1) of class 1 or a ranged class ($0413) is spent: its slot is emptied and the weapon field (+$1F) cleared; for class 13 (Grenade, Plastic explosive, TNT) another slot holding the same item becomes the weapon.
Operand of LDA #imm at $A573: the item number of the weapon attack_done has just used up (written at $A55F), searched for again with find_item to equip the next one of a class-13 item.

Attack roll of member A (select_member): 2d6 with doubles rolling again. A roll under 4 followed by a 1 on a d6 spoils the attack (carry set): classes 8, 9 and 13 'fail to detonate' (message 41), other weapons jam (message 42: count byte $80, rounds lost, roster line redrawn). Otherwise acc1 ($6F/$70) = the roll + DEX (+$13) + 4 * the weapon skill level (weapon_skill_bonus) + 10 for class 13, else +4 in burst mode or + the rounds left in automatic mode; carry clear.
Operand of LDA #imm at $A5BD: the member member_hit_roll is rolling for (written at $A584), used to redraw its roster line after a jam and read at $A5E0 for its fire mode.
A = member Y's fire mode, bits 6-7 of its order parameter ($8B),Y shifted down: 0 single shot, 1 burst, 2 automatic (member_attack and agent 8's $A02E/$A0AA; $9031 jumps to shift_right_4 inside it).
A = A >> 4: the high nibble of a byte. Shared tail of member_fire_mode; called directly for the use type of an order (order_use), a pixel line to a view row ($AEC8) and record nibbles ($9ECE, $B0B1).
Runs enter_map ($03B6) for map $8D (the map of the party being dealt with) with $09 set to it for the call, then puts $09 back. resolve_runs_and_moves calls it after moving a party.
Clears the engine's 24-bit number $1C-$1E (number_0-2), which add_experience ($03DD) adds to the current character's experience.

One hit of member A on monster line Y (0-47): picks one of the line's ten monsters at random (random_monster); carry set when that one is already dead (the caller tries again). Otherwise adds the line to the hit list $7E06 (3 entries, $FF ends it) and counts the hit ($7E12 + 10 * entry + monster), rolls the damage (weapon_damage, with the line's armour dice), sets $D7 for classes 8-9, takes off the armour (monster_armour_absorb) and adds the damage to the line's total ($7E0C, a word per entry, stops at $FFFF). Returns carry clear: A = $FF when the monster lives (or the damage was 0); A = 0 when it died: HP word cleared, $7E09 kill count + 1, its status byte (+$14) set to $FF, experience (kill_experience) given to the member, overkill flag $D9 (set_overkill), $7E30 &= $D9 and $7E33 = the line's weapon class nibble (1 if the status byte was 0).
Operand of LDA #imm at $A65C: the monster line index (0-47) damage_monster is hitting, written at $A61B; read at $A639, $A645, $A684, $A6BD and $A713.
Operand of LDA #imm at $A668: the attacking member (party position), written at damage_monster's entry ($A618).
Operand of LDA #imm at $A680: low byte of damage_monster's damage, first the roll (weapon_damage, $A66D), then the damage left after armour ($A68A).
Operand of LDX #imm at $A682: high byte of damage_monster's damage (the roll at $A670, after armour at $A68D).
Operand of LDA #imm at $A6C6: the monster (0-9) within its line that damage_monster picked (random_monster, $A628); also added to the hit counter's index ($A655) and to the status offset ($A6FD).
Operand of LDX #imm at $A6E5: the entry (0-2) of the hit list $7E06 that holds this line, written at $A64B; indexes $7E09, $7E0C, $7E12, $7E30 and $7E33.
Operand of LDA #imm at $A71C: low byte of the killed monster's HP word after the damage was taken off (0 or a negative remainder), written at $A6EC and passed to set_overkill.
Operand of LDX #imm at $A71E: high byte of the remainder (written at $A6F6), for set_overkill.

Operand of LDA #imm at $A72C, stored in $7E33 for the hit-list entry: the line's monster weapon class nibble (record byte 5 bits 0-3, written at $A6BA), or 1 when the killed monster's status byte was 0 ($A70A).

Rolls the armour of monster line A/X/Y (party, group, line, as line_index_split gives them): line_monster_record, then X = record byte 4 bits 0-3 (the armour dice) and roll_d6s_plus with A = 0. Returns the 16-bit roll in X:A.

Target number of member A's attack (member_attack, $9FD4): the distance from the party to its target group (distance_to_party), the range kind of the member's weapon class (weapon_range_kind on $7E after member_reach) and column 0 when the monster record found is of a ranged class ($0413), 1 (7 more) otherwise, through range_target ($BD48). The record is taken with X = the group number from line_index_split ($A74B), where $9E9F expects a line (0-2).
Operand of LDA #imm at $A75E: the member member_range_target works for (written at $A741), passed to member_reach.
Operand of LDX #imm at $A766: the X that line_index_split returned for the member's target (the group, 0-3), written at $A74B and given to $9E9F, which reads it as a line (0-2).

Target number for monster line X attacking at distance A (feet): the line's monster record ($9E9F), its weapon class nibble ($9ED4), weapon_range_kind, then range_target with column 0. Returns A, X = 0. Called at $84B5 and $8527 (with the distance of a group) and $9CEA.
Calls range_target ($BD48) with the distance A, kind Y and column X set by the caller, and returns X = 0.
Range kind of weapon class A for range_target: Y = 0 for classes 2, 5, 10 and 13; 1 for 3, 6, 11 and 8; 2 for every other class (1, 4, 7, 9, 12 and up). A is kept.
Attribute bonus of the current character's LK (+$10). The BITs at $A7BA, $A7BD and $A7C0 hide three more entries: $A7BB DEX (+$13), $A7BE AGL (+$12), $A7C1 ST (+$0E).
Hidden entry (inside BIT $13A0 at $A7BA): LDY #$13, the attribute bonus of DEX.
Hidden entry (inside BIT $12A0 at $A7BD): LDY #$12, the attribute bonus of AGL.
Hidden entry (inside BIT $0EA0 at $A7C0): LDY #$0E, the attribute bonus of ST.
Bonus for the current character's attribute at record offset Y, a signed 16-bit X:A: (value - 12) / 2 for 13 and up, 0 for 9 to 12, and (value - 9) / 2 rounded down (negative, X = $FF) below 9.

Damage of member A's attack: weapon_damage_roll (X = the target's armour dice), plus the member's luck bonus (luck_bonus, signed). A negative sum is not caught: it comes back as a large unsigned X:A (not checked in play).
Operand of ADC #imm at $A7EB: low byte of weapon_damage_roll's result, written at $A7E1.
Operand of ADC #imm at $A7EF: high byte of weapon_damage_roll's result, written at $A7E4.

Dice of member A's weapon (member_reach first; X = the target's armour dice). A melee weapon, or a gun with rounds, rolls its item byte 6 in d6; classes 8 and 9 roll 2 * dice - armour instead when the dice are at least the armour ($FF at most). An empty or jammed gun (reach 15) is swung: 1d6 for classes 2 and 10, 2d6 otherwise, and the class number is added (A = $7E at the JMP; the LDA #$00 at $A809 is overwritten). Result in X:A (roll_d6s_plus).
Operand of CPX #imm at $A823: the target's armour dice (X at weapon_damage_roll's entry, written at $A7F4), also subtracted at $A82C.
Operand of ADC #imm at $A830: the weapon's damage dice (item record byte 6), written at $A827, so classes 8-9 roll 2 * dice - armour.

Counts the living monsters (HP word non-zero) of monster line A/X/Y (party, group, line; group_line_ptr leaves $79/$7A on it). Carry clear with A = the count when there is one, carry set with A = 0 when none.
Operand of LDA #imm at $A853: line_alive_count's count of monsters with a non-zero HP word, cleared at $A841 and incremented at $A84D.

Party member Y takes X:A points of damage, with the messages ($C8 non-zero: not from a monster; $A0 non-zero: armour ignored). Carry set, nothing done, when the member is dead (CON 0). A member already down (CON negative) cannot be missed by $C8 damage; a monster's ranged class misses, a melee one hits when 2d6 (open) is below its record byte 3. Armour: AC (+$1A) in d6 off the damage. Then CON is reduced (con_subtract): reaching 0 makes it -1, below -49 makes it 0 (dead); a down member gets its old CON in +$26/+$27 and ' and ' + the condition message (condition_messages). Ends with '.' and the roster line; carry clear.

Operand of LDA #imm at $A892: the attacker's weapon class, the low nibble of byte 5 of the monster record at $16 ($9ED4, written at $A86E); 1 (melee) with no armour roll left gives ' but misses.' ($A8EE).
Operand of LDA #imm at $A8F5: the member's AC (+$1A), written at $A8BF; 0 with a melee attacker turns a fully absorbed hit into ' but misses.'.
Operand of LDA #imm at $A963: the member taking the damage (Y at member_takes_damage's entry, written at $A861), whose roster line is redrawn at the end.
Sets both bytes of the current character's CON (+$1D/+$1E) to A: $FF makes it -1, 0 makes it 0 (dead).
Copies the current character's record word at offset Y to $027A/$027B (member_takes_damage: the CON at +$1D, or +$26 for a member already down).

Game message numbers for condition_index 0-5: 49 'knocks him/her unconscious', 50 'seriously wounds', 51 'critically wounds', 52 'mortally wounds', 53 'knocks comatose', 25 'rips him/her to shreds' (dead).
Number of hits of member A's automatic fire (member_attack, $A0F3): select_member, the rounds left in its weapon (weapon_rounds), then auto_fire_dice.
Rolls max(1, A / 4) d4 and returns the total in A (also entered here by $9D5A with A set by the caller).
Operand of ADC #imm at $A9A4: the running total of auto_fire_dice's d4 rolls, cleared at $A994.

Combat orders for party $08 (continues s_B3B2 from $B3E9, when one of its four encounter groups exists): shows the attackers' portrait (encounter_portrait), then asks each conscious member 1 to $07 in turn for an order (message 55 and order_keys); the order is stored at ($89)+member and the handler's result at ($8B)+member. Carry set when the player backs out past the first member.

Order key space (order 0): shows the map with the roster hidden ($AC8C) until a key is pressed, then the roster and the picture window again; the portrait animation flag $AC is kept. Returns carry set, so the member is asked again.

Order key S (order 8 in order_keys, not named in the menu text): drops the dispatch's return address and continues at $B443 as Attack (order 2) with $025A = 0, so order_attack lists the groups in reach even when there is only one.

Order handler table, a word per key of order_keys (the key's index is the order): space $B489, H $B6EC Hire, A $B4C7 Attack, W $B6D8 Weapon, R $B716 Run, E $B478 Evade (CLC/RTS, no argument), L $B747 Load/unjam, U $B76E Use, S $B4A0. Read at $B44D/$B452 and run through JMP ($12) at $AC69.
Keys of the combat order prompt, for wait_listed_key at $B43E: space H A W R E L U S ($A0 $C8 $C1 $D7 $D2 $C5 $CC $D5 $D3), zero-terminated; the index is the order number 0-8.

Order A (Attack) for member A: needs a working weapon and a monster line in reach; an NPC picks a line and fire mode itself, a player character from the group list and the S)ingle B)urst A)uto question. Returns carry clear with A = fire mode * 64 + line index (0-47), carry set when refused or cancelled.

Chance of automatic fire for an NPC (order_attack, $B551), indexed by the number of characters (records 1 to $0A) who are not conscious: a d10 at or above the entry chooses A)uto over B)urst. $FF 9 7 5 3 0 0 0: never, 20, 40, 60, 80 %, then always.
Keys of the fire mode question (order_attack, $B5FE): S B A ($D3 $C2 $C1), zero-terminated; the index is the mode, 0 single, 1 burst, 2 automatic.

Shows the list of monster lines in reach for Attack and Hire: item count $4E = A + 1, title message 63 'Which group?', items 1-64 ($4D = $41) printed by group_list_line ($47/$48), none marked ($D1 = $FF), from item 1; ends in list_show_page ($03A4).

Per-item routine of the group list: item A (1-based) is the monster line A-1, split by line_index_split into party, group and line. Carry set (left off) unless group_in_reach passes and the line has monsters; otherwise prints the line label (inverse when the group is fighting the current party $08), count and name, and the distance in feet; carry clear.

Can the party reach the group record at ($79)? Carry set when it is on another map (byte 2 != $09), empty (byte 0 = 0), farther than the reach $7D, off the map window ($B119) or out of sight ($8347: a square of type 11 on the line). Otherwise $77/$78 = its square's record and A = the distance in feet.

Order W (Weapon) for member A: no items gives message 64 'You don't have anything.' and carry set; otherwise the member's item list (item_list_page), returning the chosen slot (carry clear) or carry set.

Order H (Hire): reach $7D = $FF (any distance); with no monster line on the map, message 57 'No one is within range.' and carry set; otherwise the group list (group_list_show) and the chosen line index 0-47 in A, carry clear; left-arrow returns carry set.

Order R (Run): in a party of more than one, 'P)arty or S)ingle player?' (message 36; left-arrow cancels); then 'Which way?' (ask_direction) with the map shown. Returns the direction 0-4 in A (ORed with $80 for P), carry set when cancelled.

Order L (Load/unjam): carry clear (allowed) when the equipped weapon is jammed (unjam) or when its ammunition item (item record byte 7) is carried; otherwise message 66 'can't be reloaded' (no ammunition item) or 65 'has no more clips', carry set.

Order U (Use) for member A: the Use dialog $8AD5 (item, skill or attribute); returns its A and X as A*16+X with carry clear, and stores its Y at $5BDB + the member's record number; carry set when cancelled. The roster is redrawn either way.

Health tick for every character record 1 to $0A (run every 16 time ticks, $AF7B, and by $B396): the unconscious recover a point (and wake at half of +$26/+$27, at least 1, on reaching 0), worse conditions lose a point (death below -50), the healthy heal a point every 64 or 128 ticks, and an affliction (+$28 bits 4-7) costs a point every 64 ticks.
Worsens the current character by one CON point (con_lose_one); a CON below -50 ($CE) becomes 0, which is death.
Heals the current character one CON point ($0407 with -1) unless the status byte +$28 is non-zero.
Takes one CON point from the current character: $0407 with A = 1, X = 0 (16-bit subtract from +$1D/+$1E).

One battle round, after 'Use these options (Y/N)?': 'Encounter begins...' (message 30) in the text window with slow scrolling; through $9F40, for every party on the battle map $8D: $9F70 (ranged attacks), then $9C65, $7F64 and the order handlers $9EFD; then the run orders ($A276) and $9C17/$9959 for every party; roster shown, animation on.
Portrait animation on: $AC = 1. The BIT at $B8CA hides animation_off's LDA #0.
Portrait animation off: $AC = 0 (entered behind the BIT at $B8CA).

Asks 'Which way?' with the I/J/space/L/K diagram (message 68, column 0, row 18) and waits for one of direction_keys: A = 0 north (I), 1 south (K), 2 west (J), 3 east (L), 4 space, carry clear; left-arrow returns carry set. The portrait animation is off meanwhile and restored.
Keys of ask_direction: I K J L space ($C9 $CB $CA $CC $A0), zero-terminated; the index is the direction 0-4.
Asks 'Use these options (Y/N)?' (message 70) and falls into ask_yes_no.
Waits for Y or N: Y returns carry clear; N or left-arrow carry set; other keys are ignored.

Picture for the encounter of party $08: the nearest monster line of its own groups, or of any party's, gives the picture (monster record byte 7) and its name, centred as the caption in $F4D0; with none, picture 8 and 'Ranger' (message 96). Ends in show_picture ($0419).
Finds the nearest monster line among A items from X+1 (group_list_line with printing off): carry clear with the item in $B961 and the line re-selected, carry set when none is in reach.
Tests item A with group_list_line, then puts the text cursor at column 1.
Slow scrolling on: $A8 = 1 (newline pauses). The BIT at $B9E5 hides slow_scroll_off's LDA #0.
Slow scrolling off: $A8 = 0 (entered behind the BIT at $B9E5).
A = A * 64 (six ASL): a fire mode into bits 6-7 of an Attack argument.
A = A * 16 (four ASL): the Use dialog's first value into the high nibble.
After a battle round: for every party 0-3 whose first group is on this map, writes each group's surviving monsters back to its map square (group_write_back).

Writes group X of party A back to the map: each line's live count (from the hit points, $A83C) goes into the square record's count byte, and a wiped-out line's type becomes 0. A wiped-out group changes its square (record bytes $0A/$0B) and is cleared; a group with bit 1 of record byte 9 is cleared anyway.
Announces a group: each line with monsters on its own line (count and name), then ' appear(s) at ' (message 46), the distance A and ' feet.' (message 71).
Prints monster line A of the square record at ($77): the count right-aligned in two columns (also the plural count $38) and the name ($9E5D); carry set when the line is empty.
Offsets in an encounter square's record of the monster counts of its lines 0-2: 4, 6, 8.
Offsets in an encounter square's record of the monster types of its lines 0-2: 3, 5, 7.
Measures every encounter group on the current map: for each party on map $09, each non-empty group's byte 3 = its distance in feet from that party ($04CF). Restores the current party.
Sets the ten per-monster flag bytes (+$14 to +$1D) of the three lines of group X of the current party to 1.
Clears the ten per-monster flag bytes (+$14 to +$1D) of the three lines of group X of the current party.
Changes the square of the group at ($79) from offset A of its square record ($77): $5F/$60 = $77/$78, then $042E with the group's square.
Points $77/$78 at the record of the square of the group at ($79) (bytes 0/1), keeping $5F/$60.
Points $77/$78 at the record of square X, Y ($042B, then $0428), keeping $5F/$60.
Points $77/$78 at entry A of the list of square type Y ($0428), keeping $5F/$60.
Points $79/$7A at line Y (0-2) of group X of party A: the group record + 4 + 30 * Y.
Points $79/$7A at group X (0-3) of party A (0-3): $EE00 + 376 * A + 94 * X.
Counts the monster lines in reach of member A (member_reach first).
Counts the monster lines in reach $7D across every group of parties 0 to $0B (group_in_reach and a non-zero count). Returns the count in A.

Reach of member A: 0 when not conscious; 15 feet (melee) unless the equipped weapon is of a ranged class, which gives $FE; an empty or jammed gun falls back to 15 (weapon_rounds). Sets $7E = the weapon's class (1 for melee). Returns A = $7D.
Clears the group record at ($79): 94 bytes of zero.
Rounds in the current character's equipped weapon (weapon_use_rounds with 0).
Uses A rounds of the current character's equipped weapon: returns the rounds left; a gun left empty, or jammed, sets the reach $7D to 15. Weapons without a clip return 1.
Points $89/$8A at the order table of party A ($F438 + 16 * A) and $8B/$8C eight bytes on, at its argument table.
Offsets of the four parties' order tables from $F438: 0, 16, 32, 48.
Shows one of two map messages chosen at random: the message number at record offset A+1 or A+2 of the current map ($61).
Shows the map message whose number is at record offset Y of the current map ($61), through print_map_message.
A = A + 1 or A + 2, at random.
Prints the names of the members flagged in $F3E5-$F3EB, separated by ', ' and joined by $ABB6 before the last.
Prints the name of the next flagged member (from the one in $BD2D) and moves on.
Target number for a ranged attack at distance A (feet) for weapon kind Y (0-2) and column X (0-1): builds a 21-entry table at $5A00 and looks up the first distance step at or above A.
Start values of range_target's table for weapon kinds 0-2: -5, 8, 19.
Steps of range_target's table for weapon kinds 0-2: 5, 2, 1.
Monster line index of party A, group X, line Y: (4A + X) * 3 + Y (0-47).
Splits monster line index A (0-47): A = party (index / 12), X = group (index / 3 mod 4), Y = line (index mod 3).
Rolls X six-sided dice and adds A: the 16-bit total in X (high) and A (low).

Square type 1 (table $ACF3): shows the map messages listed in the square's record (the last with bit 7 set), not again while the party stays on the same square, then changes the square from the bytes after the list ($B105).
Finds message A of the current map's text block ($031A, then find_message $0314).
Shows the map message whose number is at ($5F)+Y, unless it is 0.
Scrolls the map window one square left (rows 1-16, the bitmap two cells and the colours), for a step east ($AE73).
Scrolls the map window one square right (rows 1-16), for a step west ($AE54).
Scrolls the map window one square up (rows 3-15 to 1-13), for a step south ($AE92).
Scrolls the map window one square down (rows 2-14 to 4-16), for a step north ($AE35).
Sets up an upright scroll: colour copy kind 2, 13 rows, four extra bitmap groups, copy forward.
Sets up a leftward scroll: colour copy kind 0, two extra bitmap groups, copy forward.
Patches the engine's row copier at $DD80 for colour copy kind X (0 left, 1 right, 2 up/down) from its tables at $DDE4-$DDF2, with all RAM banked in.
Destination of a row copy: $14/$15 = the bitmap address of row Y + 8 (cell 1); the colour copy's destination = screen row Y.
Destination of a row copy with offset X (0 cell 1, 1 cell 5): $14/$15 = bitmap row Y + offset; colour destination = screen row Y.
Source of a row copy: $12/$13 = the bitmap address of row Y + 24 (cell 3); the colour copy's source = screen row Y.
Source of a row copy at cell 1 (X = 1, behind the BIT at $BF11): $12/$13 = bitmap row Y + 8; colour source = screen row Y.
The Order command (Y/N), for a party of two or more: loads the party-order program (track 34, logical sector 15, one page) to $CA00 and jumps to it. N or left-arrow redraws the map ($AC8C).
